pr.title: Don't use Immediate::offset to transmute pointers to integers
pr.description:
This applies the relatively new `assert_matches_abi` check in the `offset` operation on immediates, which makes sure that if offsets are used to alter the layout (which is possible because the field layout is arbitrarily picked by the caller), this is not done in a way that breaks the invariant of the `Immediate` type.

This leads to ICEs in a GVN mir-opt test, so the second commit fixes GVN.

Fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/131064.
pr.author: RalfJung

processing.reason:
No source-grounded original/transformed pair can satisfy the required observable-value criterion for this PR.

The historical defect is an `Immediate` invariant violation, not a value-changing optimization. Old GVN folded a pointer-source transmute by returning the existing `Scalar::Ptr` immediate under the target integer layout. On a defined execution, the actual MIR transmute and this folded immediate still denote the same address bits, so any ordinary integer use either observes the same value or must convert the `Scalar::Ptr` to an integer. In Miri/debug builds that invariant violation is exactly what `assert_matches_abi` catches (an ICE/panic); in a release-like path, converting a provenance-carrying pointer scalar to an integer either strips to the same address or reports `ReadPointerAsInt`/unsupported. Neither yields a different well-defined numeric/boolean/character result.

The other unsafe case is a `ScalarPair` whose second-component alignment differs despite equal component sizes. That condition cannot be instantiated from ordinary Rust types on the fixed host target: same-sized scalar primitives have the same alignment (and genuinely packed layouts do not provide a valid `ScalarPair` with a shifted second component). Thus it cannot be modeled by a concrete Rust input here without inventing an unrelated transformation.

Manufacturing a sentinel return value or deliberately entering a panicking/UB path would not encode the historical rewrite. Therefore the only faithful reconstruction would either produce equal values or fail to have a successful defined transformed execution.

evidence: This applies the relatively new `assert_matches_abi` check in the `offset` operation on immediates, which makes sure that if offsets are used to alter the layout (which is possible because the field layout is arbitrarily picked by the caller), this is not done in a way that breaks the invariant of the `Immediate` type.
This leads to ICEs in a GVN mir-opt test, so the second commit fixes GVN.
// `offset` for immediates only supports scalar/scalar-pair ABIs,
// so bail out if the target is not one.
// `offset` for immediates generally only supports projections that match the
// type of the immediate. However, as a HACK, we exploit that it can also do
// limited transmutes: it only works between types with the same layout, and
// The alignment of the second component determines its offset, so that also needs to match.
// None of the inputs may be a pointer.
// It is "okay" to transmute from `usize` to a pointer (GVN relies on that).
// This is not a pointer, it should not carry provenance.
(only changing the `valid_range` is allowed and turning integers into pointers).

analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation was GVN constant-folding a transmute from an immediate pointer value to a same-sized integer (or a ScalarPair with a pointer component, or with different second-component alignment) by reinterpreting the existing immediate via offset-by-zero. This preserved the pointer's provenance bits inside an immediate whose new ABI says the component must be a plain integer, violating the Immediate invariant. Such a fold must not be performed; GVN must leave the transmute in place instead. The corrected logic allows Scalar folding only when source and target sizes match and the source primitive is not a pointer; for ScalarPair it additionally requires both component sizes to match, the second components' alignments to match, and neither source component to be a pointer. The corrected comments state: `it only works between types with the same layout, and cannot transmute pointers to integers.`
analysis.inputDomain: MIR functions containing a `CastKind::Transmute` on a constant/immediate operand, where GVN can see both source and destination layouts. Paired inputs should differ only in the ABI-level property that distinguishes legal from illegal folding: (1) same-sized pointer source -> integer target (must not fold) versus same-sized integer source -> integer target, or integer source -> pointer target (may fold); (2) ScalarPair with a pointer in its first or second component (must not fold) versus ScalarPair with only integer components and matching component sizes/alignment; (3) ScalarPair with equal component sizes but different second-component alignment (must not fold). These cases should be expressed as Rust/MIR constants of Scalar or ScalarPair layout so that the transmute operand is an immediate at GVN time.
analysis.originalLogic: Before the fix, GVN handled `CastKind::Transmute` by checking only the ABI shapes: `(Abi::Scalar(..), Abi::Scalar(..)) => {}` and `(Abi::ScalarPair(..), Abi::ScalarPair(..)) => {}`; any other pair returned `None`. It then unconditionally evaluated `value.offset(Size::ZERO, to, &self.ecx).discard_err()?`. The previous `Immediate::offset` implementation therefore accepted these reinterprets as same-size projections; its ScalarPair arm even contained the comment `It is "okay" to transmute from usize to a pointer (GVN relies on that). So only compare the size.` The old code thus folded transmutes based only on matching ABI shape, without checking primitive pointer-ness, pair-component alignment, or the provenance invariant.
pitfalls: Checking only that both ABIs are Scalar or both are ScalarPair is insufficient; the source primitive and component layout details determine whether offset-by-zero is a valid reinterpretation.
For ScalarPair, matching component sizes is not enough: the second component's offset is determined by its alignment, so `b1.align(&self.ecx) == b2.align(&self.ecx)` is also required.
Only source pointer-ness is rejected for permitted folding; the range documentation allows `turning integers into pointers`, so an integer-to-pointer fold is not the invalid direction.
A pointer's provenance cannot be represented in an ABI component that is not a pointer; the `Immediate` invariant requires a non-pointer scalar to be `Scalar::Int(..)`.
The failure is not merely a size mismatch: even same-sized components can be invalid because of provenance or ScalarPair field offset/alignment.

Do not infer correctness from coverage file expectations alone; the supplied regression hunks change `.cov-map` counters (`Zero` to `Counter(3)`), while the GVN safety condition itself is in `rustc_mir_transform/src/gvn.rs`.
preconditions: The transmute operand has already been evaluated to an immediate, so GVN takes the `is_right()` path rather than operating on an mplace.
The source and target layouts each have either Scalar ABI or each have ScalarPair ABI.
For the unsafe Scalar case, the source primitive is a pointer and the target is a same-sized non-pointer type, so the resulting scalar carries provenance under a non-pointer ABI.

For the unsafe ScalarPair case, a source component is a pointer, or the second components have equal size but different alignment, changing the second component's offset while `offset` treats the operation as a same-layout projection.
The ABI invariant is enforced by `assert_matches_abi` inside `Immediate::offset` under `cfg!(debug_assertions)`.
analysis.summary: GVN's constant folding of `CastKind::Transmute` used `Immediate::offset(Size::ZERO, target_layout)` as a generic same-layout reinterpretation. It accepted any Scalar/Scalar or ScalarPair/ScalarPair pair, including pointer sources reinterpreted as integers, and ScalarPair pairs whose second component alignment (and therefore offset) differed. The new `assert_matches_abi` check in `offset_` turns these invalid immediates into ICEs in debug builds; the fix restricts GVN to legal limited transmutes and otherwise bails out without folding.
analysis.testStrategy: Add focused `tests/mir-opt` cases for GVN's transmute folding, compiling with debug assertions so `offset_`'s `assert_matches_abi` runs. Use paired programs that differ only in the ABI property: pointer-to-same-size-integer versus integer-to-same-size-integer/integer-to-pointer; ScalarPair with a pointer component versus all-integer components; and ScalarPair with equal component sizes but different second-component alignment. Assert statically that the unsafe cases keep the `CastKind::Transmute` rather than becoming a folded constant and do not ICE, while legal same-layout cases may be folded as expected. Also run the existing GVN MIR tests under debug assertions, because the PR description states this invariant check `leads to ICEs in a GVN mir-opt test` before the GVN fix. The supplied patch itself only shows coverage `.cov-map` expectation updates, not the GVN MIR test hunk, so do not treat those coverage changes as proof of the GVN rewrite.
analysis.trigger: GVN evaluates a MIR `CastKind::Transmute` whose operand is an immediate (not an mplace) and whose source and target ABIs are both `Abi::Scalar` or both `Abi::ScalarPair`; folding occurs through an offset-by-zero reinterpretation. Unsafe cases are a pointer source with an integer target of the same size, or a ScalarPair where either source component is a pointer or the second components' alignments differ despite equal component sizes.
